---
title: "How do I find the probability that A or B occurs without double-counting?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I find the probability that A or B occurs without double-counting?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Calculate the fraction for A and for B.

2. Calculate the overlap A AND B.

3. Use P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B), then check that the result is at most 1.

## Runnable example

```{r}
rain <- c(TRUE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,TRUE)
wind <- c(TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE)
p_a <- mean(rain); p_b <- mean(wind); overlap <- mean(rain & wind)
p_union <- p_a+p_b-overlap
print(c(P_A=p_a,P_B=p_b,P_both=overlap,P_either=p_union))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(p_union,mean(rain | wind))))
```

## Interpret the result

Five of eight days had rain, four had wind, and three had both. The probability of either event in this sample is 6/8 = 0.75.

## Check before using your own data

The word 'or' is normally inclusive; confirm whether the question instead requires exactly one event.
